fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Loki's Staff and the Secret Letters", "body": "Chance Garton described a Celtic god of eloquence, shown with golden chains running from his mouth to his followers, as the model for Loki, and he read Loki's scepter as a caduceus for secret communication with a black robed priest figure. He argued that secret letters were once carried on staves and that writing itself was a form of telepathy. Gabe added a cipher he learned about while studying the Voynich manuscript, a strip wrapped around a staff of fixed thickness. Chance then speculated, in his words high octane speculation, that horses might be symbolic secret messengers in Kabbalah."}, {"title": "Thor, Grief and Hero Trauma Arcs", "body": "Chance said Thor was a character many men identified with and that his collapse into grief, shown as weight gain and drinking, could plant a dangerous neural pathway in viewers who would all lose someone eventually. He asked whether trauma arcs worked as hooks that made zeroing out seem like an acceptable response. Gabe described a scene he had watched that day in which another character shook a despairing hero out of backing down. Chance also noted that Thor and Odin imagery was associated with nationalist movements, so identifying with them could draw labels. Gabe said he had once identified strongly with Thor."}, {"title": "Tony Stark as Yoni Stork", "body": "Chance explained why he had called Tony Stark Yoni Stork, reading the giant whale monsters in the Battle of New York as a cue for the story of Jonah, whose name he linked to a Hebrew word for dove. He described Tony as the dove released from the Ark and as a savior figure whose arc reactor echoed the Ark. Gabe tied Tony to the hierophant, chariot and hermit cards, saying the red and blue of the suit matched the paired sphinxes of the Rider-Waite chariot, and agreed that calling him Yoni Stork was fully allowed. Chance added that technology originally meant technical language."}, {"title": "Blue Beam Fears and the Idea of Demons", "body": "Chance said the portal in the Battle of New York was projected from a blue beam and that alien invasion fears were echoed throughout the film. Gabe argued that the blue beam operation had been running since the film Avatar, which he said primed audiences to feel sentimental about blue light. One of the hosts suggested the real alien might be a disembodied consciousness, and Chance described a holistic view in which demonic attachment could be a person's own fragmented life force energy. A chat member also posted a Hebrew term for paganism that Chance wanted to revisit."}, {"title": "AI, the Statesman and Hail Hydra", "body": "Chance read Ultron as a symbol of artificial intelligence, wondering aloud whether energy trapped in closed circuitry might be a kind of demonic construct. Gabe replied that intelligence is not consciousness and that tools can only imitate feeling. Chance described the ship called the Statesman in Infinity War as a wink from the filmmakers, and Gabe tied the Marvel Studios logo to the number ten and to what he called diablo ex machina, a satanic ending that leaves audiences without resolution. Gabe also offered a metaphor from the Hail Hydra scene, saying one drop of truth could reveal who was awake."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: In classic DeMystifiers style, one stream is never enough! Tonight we return to finish the job, exploring specific social events pre-echoed in the many Marvel Avengers movies, the leveraging of trauma to wire specific neural pathways in the audience, and the esoteric symbolism laid up in the series.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "What blows my mind about the Avengers movies is how every major scary psychological operation under the sun in the last hundred years is in some way echoed or reinforced, or, you know, the thumbs in the eyeballs pressed in deeper on these different things.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Yoni symbolism is dove symbolism, they go hand in hand, and the yoni, the dove being released from the Ark in so many different versions of the myth, is the point of course where we know that we've been saved.
